plan: candidate0008 keeps the proven native-equivalent FP32 forward and fuses only the backward. The forward reproduces _NativeAutocastCrossEntropy.forward math and operation ordering EXACTLY (logits.float -> max -> in-place subtract_ -> gather index -> exp(out=) -> sum -> log -> div_), omitting only the three world_size==1 all-reduces (MAX/SUM/SUM) as TP1 identities; it is native Torch, not a Triton forward fusion. This returns the EXACT native FP32 loss and FP32 softmax probabilities and leaves the BF16 input logits bitwise unchanged (logits.float() copies for BF16 input; aliases for FP32 input, preserving the native observable in-place overwrite). Only the backward is fused into one Triton launch of the inherited _ce_backward_kernel, which reuses the saved FP32 softmax buffer in place and computes (prob - onehot) * grad_output in FP32: onehot subtracted in FP32 THEN multiplied by the FP32 upstream, exactly matching native grad -= softmax_update; grad.mul_(grad_output) two-step rounding. The launch passes enable_fp_fusion=False and falls back without it if Triton 2.1.0 does not accept the kwarg; the expression mul(sub(prob,onehot),grad_output) has no add-of-product, so no FMA contraction is possible even on the fallback path. Out-of-range labels (including -100, NOT ignore_index) reproduce native's skipped subtraction because the raw int64 label matches no in-range lane, so no mask tensor is needed. Autograd casts the FP32 dlogits back to BF16 natively. Under active CUDA autocast it still dispatches to the fully native CE (zero Triton launches, exact loss/dlogits), preserving the 0006 autocast repair. Compiled cache stores only Triton code objects/metadata keyed by device/vocab/block/alignment booleans.
lineage: Parent candidate0007 (non-autocast path fully fused the Triton forward, widening BF16 logits in-kernel into an FP32 probability buffer and computing softmax in the kernel) FAILED the true-BF16 three-step fixed tolerance at step2/output, step2 position_embeddings wgrad, step3/output, step3 linear_proj.weight wgrad and step3 position_embeddings wgrad: the in-kernel reduction/exp/div ordering diverged from Torch, perturbing the BF16 dlogits, and FP32-master SGD parameter re-rounding amplified the drift across steps. candidate0008 reverts the forward to the 0006 _NativeAutocastCrossEntropy native Torch math/ordering (now used for both the autocast and the non-autocast branch) to remove all forward roundoff, and keeps ONLY the inherited _ce_backward_kernel for a native-equivalent fused backward (enable_fp_fusion=False when supported). Lineage 0003(residual/RMSNorm prefix) -> 0005(Triton forward, autocast re-round failures) -> 0006(autocast native repair) -> 0007(removed forward .float launch, fully fused forward) -> 0008(native forward, backward-only fusion). The residual/RMSNorm prefix is excluded; this standalone source is CE-only.
semantic_risks: The fused backward relies on BI-V150/CoreX4.2 Triton FP32 subtract and multiply being IEEE-754 correctly rounded so that (prob - onehot) * grad_output bit-matches native's two-step grad -= softmax_update; grad.mul_(grad_output). If the FP32 ALU path deviates, dlogits and the downstream FP32-master SGD updates could exceed atol 3e-4 / rtol 1e-3 and reject the candidate, as any fused-backward discrepancy does.

enable_fp_fusion=False may be unsupported in Triton 2.1.0; the code falls back to a plain launch. Correctness on the fallback depends on mul(sub(prob,onehot),grad_output) having no add-of-product pattern for the backend to contract into a single-rounded FMA. If the backend still contracts it, single rounding would diverge from native two-step rounding.

Out-of-range and -100 labels are handled by passing the raw int64 target to the kernel and relying on (col == target) never matching for negative or >= V labels. If the in-kernel int64 comparison truncates, wraps, or an unexpected label coincides with an in-range lane, an erroneous onehot subtraction would occur, unlike native which zeroes masked_target and softmax_update.

grad_output and target are assumed contiguous row-major with rows = S*B aligned to prob's [S,B,V] flattening (offset = row*V + col; GRAD_OUTPUT+row; TARGET+row). Non-contiguous inputs would misindex; the protected adapter is relied on to guarantee contiguity.

The kernel aliases the saved FP32 softmax buffer as both PROB input and DLOGITS output. Correctness relies on each program reading its own row before overwriting it and never touching another row, so the in-place reuse (matching native's in-place softmax overwrite) is safe only under this one-row-per-program invariant.

The forward is exact native Torch, but any residual numerical divergence must originate solely in the fused backward. If BI-V150 native reductions in the forward (torch.max/exp/sum/log/div_) themselves differ from the CPU float64 reference, those still gate and are outside this candidate's control.

BLOCK = next_power_of_2(vocab) uses a masked tail: masked lanes load other=0.0 and are not stored. This assumes the store mask reliably suppresses out-of-bounds writes for the padded lanes on this CoreX build.

Dispatch depends on torch.is_autocast_enabled() correctly reflecting CUDA autocast state; if a different autocast API or device autocast is active, the branch selection (native-only vs fused-backward) could be wrong, and the autocast audit expectation of zero Triton launches could be violated.
